utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, since all the technical problems seems -- seem to have been solved, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. On my list are two requests to address the Chamber. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I think you were the first. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, and Your Honours, thank you. The reason why we wanted to address your Chamber is the following: It seems to be that there is a degradation which is very regrettable, and that is what the Defence does not wish to have, which is a bad relationship between the parties. It seems to be, that is what the Defence thinks, that the Prosecution's policy is to waste as much time as possible while the Defence is presenting its case. The Defence underscores first that yesterday after the session immediately we had a meeting with the section assisting the witnesses, and they were complaining about the fact that some witnesses were staying here for a very long time without being able to testify here. I apologise. I am sorry. Thank you. Without being able to testify here before your Chamber because the sessions were continuing and developing in unsatisfactory fashion. This is very symptomatic in terms of what is happening. We know and we have already had this as a problem before this Chamber that in all the languages there is a problem of homonymy. In French, for instance there is "Dupont" and "Dupond" and of course the way we write these names, family names, and we also have this in Serbian. There are many people called Milosevic, many people called Dragan. As far as this witness is concerned, the one that we are hearing today, and as far as the document that he was questioned about yesterday, the famous report consisting of some 20 pages, the Prosecution couldn't have possibly overlooked the fact that if they were going to give us this document, there would be a break in the proceedings because the Defence wanted to see what was happening and to find out in detail what was going on and to confer with the accused. However, if only there was just a precaution taken to have a look at it beforehand, and just asking the witness, were you there at this time during these events, were you accused or charged in such-and-such a case, then immediately the situation would have been clarified. And the situation would have been even more clarified because considering that the testimony under oath this witness said that he was in the trenches in his area in Dobrinja. We know perfectly well in the proceedings the distance which is real between Dobrinja I, II, III and IV and we know during the war that the road between these locations is even longer because one had to go in a roundabout way, and this problem of homonymy was there from the start. Now, considering that the Prosecution did not want to proceed this way, this was putting Defence in a very difficult position and the Defence wishes to be categorical on this point saying that in this way, we are doing two things. First of all, the Defence is being upset through in the presentation of its case and they have succeeded in that. The second thing, and this is even worse we are trying to put pressure on the witnesses because the witnesses, who are waiting not knowing what is going on, sometimes even half an hour, hours waiting, are certainly not in a very good position to come and tell the truth before the Chamber. Now, if this is going to be accepted, this is going to be something completely rotten, and I am sorry that I am using this but that is exactly what is going to happen. Now, the second point that I have to underscore, is that if the Defence is trying as much as it is, and as it is doing now, to intervene with the Prosecution and ask questions in writing, the Defence would like to have some answers. If we are saying, for such-and-such a meeting we want to do such-and-such a thing, could we please have an answer. Could we have a reply rather than pretending that there has been no steps taken on our side. We do not think that this is something that is going to speed up the -- this case. And it is not going to ensure a proper proceeding. This is what I wanted to say, Mr. President. As far as the time is concerned that we had to use in order to treat the problem of useless document yesterday this time should definitely be taken off the time of the Prosecution, and it should not be necessary that any other calculation should be done considering that the proceedings have been carried out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Mr. Ierace, you also asked a possibility to address the Chamber. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Firstly, we don't have LiveNote, so perhaps while I speak, we can have some assistance. Secondly, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, page 3, line 13 has referred to the -- an allegation that the Prosecution is not assisting him with meetings. I do not know what he is referring to so I can't respond to that. One of the concerns expressed by Mr. Piletta-Zanin in what he just said is that he has a backlog of witnesses and there has been some concern expressed by the VWU to him about that. I think that the Defence should look again at the witness timetables which they have given to the Prosecution, the Trial Chamber, because it is apparent from those that there is no allowance for cross-examination. The Defence is relying only on its examination-in-chief times in order to construct its timetable. They sometimes have two witnesses down for the one day with two hours of testimony marked as expected for each of those two witnesses. So there is simply no allowance for them to be dealt with properly. So that is the fundamental problem, I think, with the timetable. Mr. President, Mr. Piletta-Zanin has also suggested that there is a bad relationship between the Defence and the Prosecution. I really don't wish to engage in that type of debate. There isn't, from our point of view. There have been a number of allegations made by the Defence in writing and in court over the previous few weeks, allegations that we have lied, that we have abruptly cancelled meetings. None of it is true. I don't propose to go into any further detail. Mr. President, the reason that I wanted to address you is that yesterday we were informed that Mr. Mundis is allowed only an extra 30 minutes of cross-examination. This gives rise to two issues. You may recall that on two occasions I have addressed you at length over the last few weeks with the proposal which I might perhaps refer to as "the banking proposal" in terms of the way in which the Prosecution conducts its cross-examination, that is that overall examination, that is cross-examination not exceed the combination of examination-in-chief and re-examination. I note that both times I have done that, the Trial Chamber has not responded, has not approved of it or indicated that it is not acceptable. I would be grateful if the Trial Chamber would respond to that and if you are against the Prosecution, the Prosecution's proposal, I would also be grateful for reasons. I would -- that would be helpful to the Prosecution in the way it structures its response to the Defence case, to have an indication as to whether that is an acceptable way for us to conduct ourselves in terms of time limits. If one looks at the times so far, leaving aside the current witness and leaving aside the witness who is part heard who is to be recalled in December, then the Prosecution has some four hours in credit. In other words, we have taken four hours less than the Defence when you combine Defence examination-in-chief and re-examination. And they are rough figures, but they are not gross figures. In other words, where there have been long discussions rather than the taking of evidence from witnesses, discussions in excess of five minutes, those times have been excluded. The second issue is that if one looks at the half hour allowance Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. on the basis of the approach which applied up until now, that is that the cross-examiner is allowed no more time than the examiner in chief took, then there is also a considerable discrepancy. Last night, I took the draft LiveNote transcript which gives times and looked at it closely. I excluded virtually all interventions and it transpires from the figures that the Prosecution has remaining one hour and 12 minutes if its time is to match the time that the Defence was allowed in terms of examining this witness. Because there is such a discrepancy between that time and the half hour that we have been allocated, I would be grateful if the Trial Chamber would reconsider that half hour allowance. Mr. President, our position is particularly difficult because we are hearing for the first time in court evidence which is contradictory to the Defence position up until this point, and again, in relation to this witness, two examples will suffice: The position of the confrontation lines and some aspects of the use of the church. There are, in other words, substantial matters that we still we wish to cross-examine this witness on. We see, for instance, that he has marked the front line position on which he operated as including the airport. There has been much in the Prosecution case about the targeting of civilians who cross the airport at night. Thank you, Mr. President. It was pointed out to me that I have inadvertently referred to the Defence where I should have referred to the Prosecution. That appears -- excuse me -- on page 6 at line 14, that is, we have heard evidence which is -- I am sorry, in fact that is what I intended -- which is contrary to the Defence position and I, in saying that, have in mind the Defence position based on contrary propositions not being put to Prosecution witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is how we understood your observation. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, one or two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you very much, Mr. President. First thing, I am making this observation that bearing in mind what the Prosecution said, they don't know what I am saying, what I am talking about. There is no comment. This is a letter from the 21st of October certainly in a language of the Tribunal, so I am still asking for a courteous answer. Now, as far as the rest is concerned, Mr. President, every party is free, as you have said to use the time as they wish. And the Prosecution has a huge advantage over the Defence because it is represented by the people who come from originally from the Anglo-Saxon law and they know exactly what the consequences of their acts and strategies are. The Prosecution wanted to undermine the credibility of this witness asking him questions regarding his credibility. This has been a complete defeat for the Prosecution. Was it the fault of the Defence? It wasn't, but the time was wasted. If the Prosecution had used this time to advance its case, we would not have been here. The second point saying that useful interventions is not necessary of General Galic, because -- General Galic, the Defence, because certainly we knew that the Prosecution had to go on to another subject. We think this is opening the door to all kinds of abuses of the proceedings and this is not the first time. I would like to remind you, for instance, witnesses, I believe DP6, the Prosecution presented the same arguments, they wanted to say how -- whether there were shooting at the trees to get rid of the leaves. We cannot accept this. We are either talking about the facts or not and so on. Now as far as the lines are concerned, we have always said that no agreement was possible on the question -- on the matter of the lines because our witnesses would come and say that the lines were not as what the Prosecution said. So this is not something which is new. If the lines were completely established then we would have already had the agreements. We have contested -- just 30 more seconds, please, please. Thank you. We have contested fully the testimony of the Chief of Staff, General Karavelic, and after, if you remember when we submitted other maps to him, he rejected him and he said that these maps were no good, that these were made by incapable people. So we couldn't use them because his point was that this was done by people who didn't know anything about it. Now, every time we could, we contested the positions, the lines of the Prosecution witnesses. Now, as far as the tower is concerned, this is my very last point, this is the fact that the Prosecution should have known, they should have told us, and the Prosecution should have asked questions of the witness themselves if the tower wasn't already destroyed and could not have been used by a sniper because there was no protection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, we are not at this moment evaluating the evidence. I think it is clear your position. Sometimes it strikes me how good both parties know what the other should do and at the same time seems to function unsatisfactorily in view of the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is just a little request because sometimes it is a little disagreeable. Could we just move the folders because I cannot see everyone and I don't know whether I am being addressed or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We could ask Madam Registrar to -- if you need any help, Madam Registrar. Yes. Now, I even can see General Galic which was fine also.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have two different issues at this moment. First of all, the relation between the parties whether they behave towards each other in such a way that it is acceptable. And that is mainly outside of court. If there is any problem in that respect, if meetings are held in such a way that no progress is made, if parties blame each other for misbehaving or -- then there is an easy solution. I will assist the parties in the meetings and since I am usually in court during five hours a day and since I have other work to do as well, these meetings would take place at 7.30 in the morning. So if any of the parties thinks that assistance is needed, they can call me and the next morning we will meet for all practical matters at 7.30 in the morning. That is as far as practical matters are concerned. Then the time calculation as far as witness DP9 is concerned, I have as data here -- let me just have a look. For DP9, I have examination-in-chief by Ms. Pilipovic for half an hour on the first day. Then examination-in-chief by Ms. Pilipovic yesterday for another 15 minutes. Then I have examination-in-chief by Mr. Piletta-Zanin for 25 minutes, that makes it all together two hours. Then I have cross-examination by Mr. Mundis up until this moment for 40 minutes yesterday before the break, half an hour after the break that would make 70 minutes up until now. 50 [Realtime transcript read in error "15"] minutes remaining. When I said 30 minutes yesterday, I deducted some time for the extra time needed to read the document which I thought at that time was not a very efficient way of using the time. I cannot give you a decision now on whether the banking system would be a good solution, but perhaps the Chamber should express itself on that. Let's just ask the witness to come in. I think, as a matter of fact, but that is a very practical matter, the discussion on the time still to be taken takes just as much time as the time you might need. So sometimes perhaps, as the parties might have experienced, we are not that rigid if the comes to the final five or six minutes. So if there would be 50 minutes available, but your calculation is a bit different.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Especially in relation to the cross-examination by Mr. Mundis yesterday. That seems to be the problem. Where you have 70 minutes, Mr. Present, I have 40. That is quite a difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that. Of course, I rely on the information I got from the Registry, and there of course it depends on what you deduct and what you do not deduct and whether an objection should be deduced or not. And that is also a matter of, I would say, of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. assessment and interpretation of the usefulness of the -- let's just be very practical. Let's call the witness and let's start and if both parties -- you are nodding "no," Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. This was just something that I was saying to myself in relation to what you were saying. I wasn't speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Be very careful because before you are nodding "no" to yourself, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, because that is a risky adventure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Mr. President, it has disappeared, but page 10 line 2, is "50," 5-0, and not "15."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, 50 minutes, 5-0, that is correct. Let's just start. Let's see whether the parties could try to work as efficient as possible and see where we come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. Please be seated, Mr. DP9.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave the day before yesterday. Mr. Mundis, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Mundis: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask with the assistance of the usher that the witness be shown Defence Exhibit 1771, and while that is being done --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, was your platoon mobile or did it remain more or less static throughout the period from September 1992 through August 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was mobile.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask you to take a look now at the map, Defence Exhibit 1771. You've indicated on this map the SRK line as it existed during the relevant time period, that is, September 1992 through August 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In light of the fact that your platoon was mobile, did your platoon operate at various times during that period across the entire length of that confrontation line or only in selected parts of that confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along certain parts of that confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness be handed a thin blue marker.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you would please place blue X's along the -- those parts of the SRK confrontation line that your platoon operated on during this period. If you could place the blue X's right on top of the solid black line that you drew yesterday.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, Witness. During the time period from September 1992 through August 1994, based on the markings you have made on the map, it's correct that your platoon was at three different locations along the confrontation line then; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to the last X that you made, that is the one at the top or the north-eastern part of the confrontation line. Can you please point to that with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. That building that you are pointing to, that entire building was on the SRK side of the line; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The rectangular building to the south-west of the building that you just indicated was also entirely on the SRK side of the confrontation line; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean this building?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was as well, but I wasn't in that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please place blue circles around both of those buildings.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the record the witness has drawn one large oval around both of the buildings in question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did your platoon have a fixed headquarters, that is a specific building where your platoons headquarters was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The platoon did not have a fixed headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that the platoon commander operated with the platoon along the three points that you have marked with an X along the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We weren't at all three of these parts at the same time that I have marked, but at different time periods. And the platoon commander was present either with the part of the platoon he was with or in the company command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday you told us that behind the SRK lines, that is, towards the rear, your unit had its logistical and support components. Do you remember telling us that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are the area or areas where these logistical units were located from September 1992 through August 1994, are those areas visible on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please place blue -- a blue X or X's at the location where the logistical support units were located in the rear areas.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you please circle the two X's that you have just made and next to the circles write the letter "L."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You also mentioned yesterday that there were former barracks in the area towards the rear of your lines. Is that former barracks visible on this map or the location of that former barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you told us yesterday that Bosnian Serb civilians who lived in this area were also relocated back from the front lines for their own safety. Are the areas where these civilians were relocated visible on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The civilians who abandoned their homes because of the combat operations went to different areas, and I really don't know where they were relocated to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the location of your company headquarters was during this time period September 1992 through August 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please place an X on the map where your company headquarters was located.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please circle that X and next to it write the letters "COHQ." "COH" and if there is no "Q" in your alphabet, a "Y" would be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fine. Witness, do you know the location of where your battalion headquarters was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please place an X at that location.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That location is not visible on this map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How about the location of your brigade headquarters, is that visible on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly where it was, that is, the brigade headquarters. But it wasn't in these areas, that's for sure. I know that. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you also told us yesterday that you had been to Lukavica Barracks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall how many times you visited that facility between September 1992 and August 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I went there several times, maybe four, three, or five times. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall within that overall time period, approximately when you were at Lukavica Barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Lukavica Barracks, I was there most often in 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall why you went to Lukavica Barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a health clinic in the barracks and as I had some medical problems I went there. And for a while, I was treated there at the clinic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From Lukavica Barracks to the Veljine church, the distance, as the crow flies, was between 1.000 and 1500 metres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what the distance is. Perhaps one should measure it. And it depends from which spot in the barracks, as the barracks is quite enormous.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the Lukavica Barracks compound you could see the tower of the Veljine church, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DP9, at any time did you have the occasion to meet with General Galic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any time did you have the opportunity to speak with General Galic over a telephone or field radio or any other electronic device?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any time when you were either at your positions along the front line or at Lukavica Barracks, did you ever see General Galic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing him ever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you, again, to look at D1771, the map that's to your right. Yesterday, you told us about ABiH trenches in front of the school building in Dobrinja. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please point to the school building.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please circle that building with a blue pen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And next to that write the letter "S."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DP9, during the early parts of the conflict in Dobrinja, the ABiH forces were actually in that school building, were they not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of the conflict, I don't know who was in the school at Dobrinja. I think that even for a while it was vacant and the ABiH forces were in a private house some 50 kilometers -- metres away parallel with the school close to a wood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if the ABiH forces were ever in the school building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ABiH forces were certainly in the school from 1993, I know that for sure, until the end of the combat operations in this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the confrontation lines that you've drawn on the south-west part of the school building, approximately how far were the confrontation lines apart at that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean these lines? Are you referring to these?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. From where your pen is towards the school. Towards the school. Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the location of the school to the location where you drew the "X." How far is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The width of two-track road, two-lane road and the schoolyard, it would be about 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the ABiH trench line or front line that you drew, you indicated yesterday that there was a trench along that front line; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The trench went from the school building towards the front lines towards the Bijelo Polje road. There were other trenches also across the road in front of the positions, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the area to the south-east of the school where you have drawn the ABiH line from that position to the SRK line and particularly where you've drawn the "X" towards the south-eastern portion of the map, approximately how far was that distance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean from here to here?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The distance is a bit bigger as between there is a football pitch and a clearing, about 300 metres perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall, Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to specify what the witness has said because the south-east indication is not clear enough because the line comes back towards the school. So I would like to make the transcript more precise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness pointed at the distance between the most easterly position of his platoon and the ABiH lines close to the school in a south-eastern direction. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall when those trenches on the ABiH side were dug or constructed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the period from 1993 and 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Witness, it is your testimony then that the ABiH forces left the school building and dug trenches directly towards the SRK front line during 1993 and 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that. They didn't leave the school again until the end of the war. After the trenches were dug out, some other units came there. According to information from the command, they were units that were not even within the same formation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now, you told us yesterday that the tower of the Veljine church was hit below the dome and that part of the wall fell down is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tower of the church was hit below the cupola and seriously damaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it from that answer that the upper parts of the church were completely destroyed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the dome remained on the lateral walls.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the -- did part of the church tower actually collapse; is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The front and back wall of the church tower collapsed in the top part of it just below the dome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that the church tower was totally destroyed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not entirely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What part of the church tower remained standing? And I take it by "tower" you are referring to the bell tower of the church?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am referring to the bell tower of the church.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What part of the bell tower of the church remained standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole tower remained standing. Only, as I said, the top part was seriously damaged, whereas the bottom part which hadn't been hit wasn't damaged at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that the reconstruction of the church commenced after the Dayton Agreement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, because I was already leaving by then, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember, Witness, when the Dayton Agreement was signed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was at the end of 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall if it was in December 1995, more precisely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date when the Dayton Agreement was signed. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately when after the Dayton Agreement was signed did the reconstruction work begin on the church?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it could have been in 1996 that some works on the church started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall if the work started in January or March or May or July or what month in 1996?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I really don't know. I didn't really pay that much attention to that. I had quite different problems to deal with regarding my own accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must object to this question. I think what is important to know is whether this was after the war, rather than whether it was in April, May or June. I don't really see the point of this line of questioning, the more so that the witness doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that this specification as far as months are concerned will become relevant in your next questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In the next several questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall how long it took to rebuild the church tower?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the reconstruction was done in stages and that it lasted a long time, but exactly how long I am unable to say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say, Witness, "a long time" do you mean a period of months or a period of a couple of years, two or three years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it lasted more than one calendar year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Veljine church, Witness, is in its present condition, seems to be -- the facade of the building seems to be stucco or plaster, and seems to be painted white; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The facade of the church is white, and I don't know that it was done with plaster.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough, Witness. Do you know when the building was painted white or when the colour of the church became white?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am afraid I don't know when that was exactly, but when the reconstruction was completed the facade was done at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness be shown what has been marked as Prosecution Exhibit 3753.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going to object to this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President -- excuse me, Mr. President. If we could ask the witness to remove his headphones during the course of this objection, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please give us the reason for your objection, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, this kind of exhibit seems to be in our version there is a different ERN number, but it's not here. These kind of exhibits we would like to know very precisely when did Prosecution find out about this, where did it come from, particularly for the photographs 1, 2, 3, 4, for all of them, about the work that was done on the church. The reason why we are asking this question is the following: There is a principle in the Rules which says that if there are exculpatory elements and the Prosecution knows about them, they need to hand it over to the Defence. So that the case with proceed properly and justly. We do not -- cannot imagine that they have only received these photograph as few hours or a few days ago. We think that this type of photograph about the work that was done on the church, these photographs must have been in the possession of the Prosecution some time ago. So if they have had in their files such photographs and this photograph in particular, now, for instance, if they had them during the time when they were presenting their own case. So, was it possible to see the work on the photographs or the damage?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So I take it that the Defence considers these photographs to be of an exculpatory nature and therefore they would have had to have been disclosed before.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please respond, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Present, I would prefer doing this in the absence of the witness for the simple reason that he seems to be looking at the monitor and I may have to mention some dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may, three points very briefly. The first one I would need a further elaboration from the Defence as to how exactly these photos are exculpatory or what their position is as to the nature, the exculpatory nature of these photographs to further respond to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I already ask one question about that. Usually only disclosed at a late time what one would expect that if they really are exculpatory, that the parties who considers them to be exculpatory because it introduces an exculpatory aspect in their case, so that is still a bit of a puzzle to me. So we would like to know about this later. But you may continue your --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, after Mr. Mundis has made his second and third observation, you will get an opportunity to respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The second point, Mr. President, is that as the Chamber is aware from the discussion yesterday the Prosecution was put on notice on the 21st of October, that is, some nine days ago, that this witness would be testifying about the destruction, alleged destruction of the bell tower of the Veljine church. That was completely new information to the Prosecution. We began undertaking a review of material that we have in house and as Mr. Ierace indicated to you yesterday, in the middle of the morning yesterday, we were able to obtain these photographs. Our position is that these photographs may have been disclosed earlier to the Defence, but for the fact that we had no idea whatsoever that this issue would become one which the Defence would deem to be relevant in the sense that we only discovered this nine days ago. With respect to when these photographs were taken, I can tell the Chamber that these photographs were taken in August of 1996, and the next line of questions to be put to the witness will go to that very issue as to the condition of the church in August of 1996 and whether or not these photographs accurately depict the church as it existed at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: As well as during the indictment period, Mr. President. We will put a series of questions concerning the condition of the church during the indictment period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please respond to the exculpatory nature of these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, gladly, Mr. President, I will reply to the Prosecution in application of Rule 90(H) and also I will reply to the Prosecution. We believe that if a sniper should be located anywhere in the top -- on top floors of a tower where he has no protection because of the wall, back or front, or the side walls which the witness has said disappeared, then there is no practical possibility to snipe because a sniper has to be protected. So his own protection is not ensured, so this is a very important element. Another element, Mr. President, that is what I discovered today, is that the Prosecution had these elements much more beforehand and they did not disclose them. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Now, if we had known for each of the incidents in Dobrinja, for instance, that this happened from the tower, if the tower -- that the tower had been damaged, then we would have been able to ask a line of questions of exculpatory character asking the witness saying, "isn't it true that this tower was open and it was not possible to place the snipers there. Wasn't it true that if a sniper was there, then the tanks from the Jusuf barracks would immediately fire and shoot the -- shoot them down." Now, we believe that these elements were intentionally hidden because they needed several hours to find them in their files. Now these exhibits show that the sniper's nest, as it is called, was not such, technically it was impossible, and we were not able to ask Prosecution witnesses about this, because this information which should have been communicated to us was not and that is the reason why we believe that it is disloyal to produce them now, especially since they are of an exculpatory nature to produce them now, because we would have wanted to have them at the time when witnesses of the Prosecution were heard. And now we retroactively underscore that we have great reserve towards this, that our rights were offended during each testimony of these witnesses because the information was not given to us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis. One short reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just a very quick comment. Mr. Piletta-Zanin in the Prosecution's submission has got the issue slightly confused. The fact of the matter is, he says that if they had known with respect to the incidents that the tower was destroyed, they would have put that to the witnesses. The fact of the matter is, we had numerous witnesses testifying about the existence of the church and the only information to date during the course of the entire trial with respect to damage to the church has come from the Defence witness, not from any Prosecution witnesses. There is, to date with the exception of this witness, there has been no evidence whatsoever that this church tower was damaged in any way whatsoever. And second of all, if I could just draw to the attention of the Chamber that this witness has just testified that from Lukavica Barracks, the church tower was visible and I don't push that issue any further other than to point out that Lukavica Barracks was the headquarters of the accused. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, just briefly on the observations made by Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand anything any more and I have to admit it. Because if I find myself in a legal position and I see a photograph with considerable works on all four of the sides, with all the work that is being done, although I am not an architect, we can see that there were considerable damages, since there was considerable work. Now the Prosecution is saying that these questions cannot be put to the witnesses in the fact that the Defence doesn't know anything about this, and perhaps because I am speaking in French I am being misunderstood, but I believe that I am sufficiently clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's just -- I do see that the mere fact that works are done at the church are considered by the Defence to be exculpatory where as the Prosecution says that it was only through Defence witnesses that attention was paid to what I would say was a substantial damage to the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may, I believe there is a misunderstanding here about the nature of the scaffolding that is visible in the photo as well as the crane that can be seen. I would simply like to draw to the attention of the Trial Chamber the testimony of, in particular, two witnesses. The first one being Ismet Hadzic and in particular the Word transcript at page 12250 and the testimony of Refik Sokolar again the Word transcript, page 3622, both of those witnesses testified and there are other witnesses I can say too, as well, both of those witnesses testified that the church had scaffolding on the tower throughout the period of the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's not in my recollection at this very moment, but I take it that since the sources have been given, that the Defence could check the correctness of the observation just made. Well, the Chamber, of course, is not in a position to give any decision at this moment without having heard at least the questions and the answers of that witness. If it would turn out that in violation of the Rules, the photographs has not been disclosed at an earlier stage, we have to see what decision should be taken in that respect. But we will first allow the Prosecution to continue. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated. Thank you for your patience, Mr. DP9. Mr. Mundis, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Again I would ask that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 3753.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the building in the centre of the photograph that is before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Orthodox church in Veljine or one of its parts, the tower.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please take the thin blue marker and circle what you have described as "the tower."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Previously you've talked about a part that you have referred to as "the dome." Is the part that you have referred to as "the dome" visible in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the visible dome of the church, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you use the term "dome," are you referring to the extreme top of the bell tower?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On its roof.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The roof of the bell tower is what you have referred to as the dome; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please place a circle around the dome.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Inside that circle, please write the letter "D."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the photograph before you, can you please mark that part of the bell tower which was destroyed by the tank fire.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here you can only see a part of the damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Inside the circle that you've just drawn, please place an "X."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The area inside the circle with the "X" in it, Witness, is that the only part of the bell tower that was damaged?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object to this question for a very good reason: Is that the witness said we can only see one part of the damage. So if we only see one part of the damage, therefore -- okay, very well, very well I don't say anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... the photograph, and the logic of possible answers is a different matter and if you would like to make such remarks, then we should ask the witness to take off his earphones. So if you think you should stand by your objection, then we have to ask the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please put his microphone on. Counsel, microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Taking off the headphones, in case we are using words that are recognisable on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this witness said earlier, asked by question is that what was on the photograph was not Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. all of the damage. Now, if it is only this damage that existed, if what we asking -- if we put this question then it is contradictory to what he testified already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please respond to the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe the question was: "Was that the only part of the bell tower that was damaged?" I can certainly show the witness additional photographs from this packet and ask him to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the -- let me just try to find it. Yes, it is not quite clear because the answer was: "Here you can only see a part of the damage" without clear reference to -- Let me ask you, Witness DP9, when you said -- yes. When you just told us that this was the only part of the damage you could see, did you intend to say that this was only part of the damage done to the bell tower that you could see or that this was only part of the damage done to the church as a whole? So bell tower and other parts of the church as well that you could see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were other damages on the church, and this is just some of the damage that we can see on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but some of the damage of what? Some of the damage to the bell tower or some of the damage to the church as whole? I mean, was there other damage done to the bell tower? Or was the other damage on other parts of the church --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I think that one part can also be seen on this photograph if we look at it very closely. In the background you can see the light, which means that the back wall has also been destroyed by the shelling when the church was shelled. And a commission of priests and civilians came and also with an officer, commission of the army because this was a facility --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me stop you there. You say we see damage at the front wall just below the dome, but you say since you can see light, there is also damage at the other side of the bell tower. Was there more damage on the bell tower, apart from the front and the back wall you just referred to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The pillars for the bells were also damaged on the inside, and also the inside of the bell tower was also damaged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But on the outside of the bell tower, there was no more damage. Is that how I am to understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lower down what you can't see on this photograph, there is another damage caused by a rocket launcher but you cannot see this detail on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because it is hidden by the bush or is that the reason why you can't see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You cannot see it because of the bushes. It is hidden by the bushes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am simply to say, we have looked at the hour. Even if we take ten minutes off, we now believe that we are much further than the half an hour that was given earlier. We just wanted to state this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do agree with you, that it takes more than the half hour granted. As you noticed, the Prosecution stressed once again that the banking system should be used. Let me just confer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just before your decision, I just want to say that the banking system was not proposed by the Prosecution during its case, and we did not have this opportunity during the Prosecution case. So I think that things should always seem to be fair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, in banking terms, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the banking system consists of building up credit. If you would look at the building up of credit in your case, I am afraid that the bank would have been closed to you. On the average, you used 20 more hours from the Prosecution and that almost on from the beginning. I don't think it would have greatly assisted the Defence to use the banking system. We give no final decision on that, but you may at least continue on until the break and we will then more thoroughly discuss it. Mr. Mundis, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DP9, do you -- let me begin again. Witness DP9, the photograph that you see before you was taken from the area controlled by the ABiH during the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, based on the condition of the building, the brush that you see and trees in the foreground and the condition of the white building on the right-hand side of the photograph, do you have any rough idea of when this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that it was made from summer of 1992 until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Witness, this photograph that you see before you accurately depicts the Veljine church throughout the period from September 1992 through August 1994, and in fact, up until the end of the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would ask you just to look at the remaining photographs that comprise Exhibit 3753, just take a moment and look at those photographs, please. Witness DP9, do all five of the photographs that you just looked at, Prosecution Exhibit 3753, do all of those photographs accurately depict the condition of the Veljine church from September 1992 through the conclusion of the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These photographs depict one side of the church and all of the photographs show the same side of the church.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough, Witness. But the question was: Do they reflect the condition of the church from September 1992 through the conclusion of the war?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I -- the witness tells us that you can only see one side. Is it your question that it depicts only that side damage --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you then --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what is visible in the five photographs, the visible part of the church, is that an accurate reflection of the state of the church with respect to those parts which are visible from September 1992 through August 1994, and in fact, to the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the church in Veljine and this side that we can see, this is what it looked like in the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Witness, all of the photographs in P3753 were taken from areas that, during the war, were controlled by forces of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DP9, looking at the first photograph in the bundle, to the left of the Veljine church, we see what appears to be a construction crane. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, was that crane at that location throughout the war or at least from September 1992 onwards until the conclusion of the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crane, the construction crane was there before the war and during the war. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Present, I note the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. How much time would you still need, Mr. Mundis, since we have to consider how much time should be granted?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will review my notes during the break, but I would think 15 to 20 minutes I could complete this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will consider whether such time will be granted to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding this question, two things. What we would want for the Prosecution to do, if you allow it, is to use the break to find out when exactly this photograph was taken. I think that is the least of the things that we should know, exactly, so that we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... said by the Prosecution in the absence of the witness. We are not going to repeat it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: But, Mr. President, might I inform you that I informed Mr. Piletta-Zanin yesterday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, apart from whether you did it yesterday, the Chamber even knows because it has been said by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the second point is that we believe that the Prosecution has gone well beyond the time allocated. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As far as time is concerned, the Chamber does not adopt generally the banking system. It is not a matter of building up credit and then use that credit at a later stage. The Chamber will, as it has done also during the presentation of the Prosecution case, always take into consideration all circumstances, that would mean as a starting point, the time used for the examination-in-chief, but also sometimes the importance of the issues on which the witness was questioned by the cross-examining party, also the way the time has been used until that moment. So we take into consideration everything all together, and the Chamber is always open for, if there are any miscalculations, please tell us. On the other hand, we are no accountants, we are no bookkeepers, but we try to keep it as strict as possible, but always in view of what happens during the examination of the witness. Then in respect of this witness, so having considered everything the way the time was used, a lot of details on positions for half an hour approximately, but on the other hand, the importance of other issues that have been raised that there is not more than 10 minutes available to the Prosecution from now on. Mr. Usher, could you -- yes, Mr. Ierace

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, thank you for the reason why the banking system is not adopted. There remains an issue as to the methodology in being applied in determine the times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: One solution to that is for the Prosecution to produce a hard copy of the transcript indicating what times the Prosecution thinks have been taken by the Defence and Prosecution. That method would allow any party to check the methodology used by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If the parties would provide the Chamber with their view on what is the time used, of course they can always submit it to the Chamber. You said that earphones off the time used or not, witness out of the courtroom, is that time used or is it not time used. It also depends on the kind of objections, the reasonableness of the objection. So there are a lot of circumstances to be taken into consideration, and if the parties would disagree and would do the bookkeeping for the Chamber. As you know the most accountants, how do you call this, the auditor firms, they would also review on whether the bookkeeping is not only correct but whether it is in accordance with the rules. So I am not saying that the Chamber will be the auditor, but it could assist under circumstance where the parties greatly disagree on the time spent, and we will then take that into consideration among all the other factors I just mentioned. So it is not -- we are not a bookkeeping firm here. At this moment I haven't taken into consideration. In this respect now, it is 10 minutes for this witness, so that's the decision of the Chamber for the moment, not more than 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I don't contest that, of course, Mr. President, but do I understand you to be saying that the 10 minutes is based on a comparison with the time taken by the Prosecution and an interpretation of the relevant --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the interpretation of the relevance and the time used and many many factors.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I should put a bonus on effective use of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have no English translation at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... time in that manner. We cannot definitely, we cannot do what you have suggested. I am so sorry for that, but I don't have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am not suggesting anything. If the parties want to submit anything in that respect, that they are free to do so. Please, Mr. Usher, could you escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP9, please be seated. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I would ask that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 3274D.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday you were asked about some buildings that appear below the blue arrow marked on this photograph. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The buildings visible below the blue arrow were not at that location or weren't present during the war; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout the war and before the war, there were private houses there of the airport locality, the Airport Settlement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know approximately how far from the place this photograph was taken that Airport Settlement is located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The locality that is shown here is located at the end of this avenue which could be at some distance of about perhaps 400, 500 metres. I wouldn't be able to tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the area of the Airport Settlement that is visible beneath the blue arrow in the photograph do you know which side of the conflict controlled that part of the Airport Settlement during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One part, one half on this side by the buildings of the Dobrinja V and III were held by the BH Army forces and the rest towards Nedzarici was under the control of the Republika Srpska Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please use the pointer, not the pen, the pointer and point to that area visible that was controlled by the VRS.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot see it on this photograph, this part held by the Republika Srpska Army. It is hidden by these buildings here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That photograph may be returned to the Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Earlier this morning, Witness, you marked three X's along the SRK confrontation line in Dobrinja where your platoon was deployed during the war. Do you remember doing that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From any of those locations could you see the Sarajevo airport Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. runway?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Sarajevo airport runway could only be seen partially in the part known as Donji Kotorac which is on the line, located on the line held by the Republika Srpska Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any time during the period from September 1992 through August 1994, were you at a position along the SRK controlled confrontation line where you could see the airport during night-time hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No I was not at those positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any time during the period September 1992 through August 1994, did you have an occasion to view the Sarajevo airport runway during night-time hours or after sunset, more specifically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't observe that no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DP9, yesterday you told us that you met with two people from the defence team in the spring of this year. The woman's name was Snjezana Prodanovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that is correct. Her first name was Snjezana, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the gentleman's name was Milenko Radovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the last name is Radovic and I believe his first name is Milenko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: One moment, please. No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. I see that you only took six minutes. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We will try and be very brief. I have two questions in connection with the questions put by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Re-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you were asked about the destruction of the top part of this tower, and my question is the following: The areas destroyed, did they face the positions held by the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I am talking about the high points of the tower, on that side had the wall entirely disappeared or not? Could you describe that for us, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The walls had partially disappeared on the upper part of the bell tower.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you know this part without walls, could it be easily hit by the opposing party on the territory controlled by the BH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your testimony, Witness, you used the word "suicide." Under these particular circumstances that you have described, would that apply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. My recollection was that that was during direct examination and not during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite right, yes. But as we are now -- and I think that the Prosecution put questions regarding this part of the facade -- and this witness having referred to suicide, I thought it was appropriate to connect the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the destruction of the church was in general terms an issue that was dealt with by the Defence during examination-in-chief. So that would make it already questionable whether any additional questions, unless there would be very specific new elements, I would say that this is not a new element, especially because if you are talking about suicide, that is exactly the words used during the examination-in-chief. Apart from that, you said you had two questions. This was the fourth one. If you have one more question, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't think that I said that I had only two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what -- let me just have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may have said two or three questions which is an expression, my manner of speech.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That stands for 20 or 30? No, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you have one -- if you have another question in relation to an issue that has been raised for the first time in the cross-examination, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will have only a few.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think following a question put to you by the Prosecution, you spoke of a sniper. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As this question was raised by the Prosecution, do you know of a person who might have been wounded in the area controlled by your army and I imply the whole area, the whole zone by sniper fire coming from the other side?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness remove his headphones, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please take your headphones off. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The question seems to go to ABiH sniping into SRK controlled areas and that was certainly not a topic that was raised by the Prosecution during its cross-examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes Mr. President. But if this witness, as he said saw sniper rifles I think it would be logical to ask him whether there were any on the other side. Maybe he saw them on the other side. And this question hasn't been put to him. And whether he might know were the people close, not so close to him were hit by a sniper. It seems to me quite logical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Questions are allowed in relation to issues that were raise for the first time in examination-in-chief. If you would give this a very wide interpretation you could re-open the case because for similar reasons, you could say if you saw rifles, you would have to know whether there was any other weaponry, so that would open the way to questions about machine-guns or even mortars. One question in this respect I will allow to you, but in general if sniping is used --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I was saying, Witness, do you know of any people on this side of the line, that is your side, may have been hit by sniper fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were such cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you perhaps give us some information about it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this contested by the Prosecution that people were hit by snipers at the side of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That is not contested, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So there is no need to ask further questions to that, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Thank you very much.
