Mr. President, the last question I should like to put to the witness has to do with certain instructions because many questions have been put to this witness about hierarchy and orders, and I have only one question in that same area, if I may. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, questions have been asked about orders. Did you receive any precise instructions not to affect civilians, and if so, on what occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such orders were issued many times, I don't know how frequently, and they were repeated from time to time. I don't know why because it was Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. sufficient to say it once. Maybe somebody had intervened or something had happened to prompt this, but I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as far as you know, were those orders respected?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along the part of the front line that I held, together with men who were present with me, orders were strictly carried out and observed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Nieto-Navia has one or more questions for you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would like the Exhibit 1771 to be put on the ELMO. During your examination you mentioned some parking lots which were close to the ABiH area. With the pointer, could you please point to those parking lots?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Using a green or a red pen could you put an "X" on those places.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: We don't need the map any more. The President says that maybe you should put a "P" close to each of the X's. "P."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like the exhibit P3753 to be shown to the witness. That is the set of photographs. It is just for some clarification. You told us that during the war both the crane and this scaffolding was there during the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: The first photograph that you have there, the first one, you told us that photograph was taken from the ABiH-controlled area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Could you go to the last photograph. Could you point to the dome, to the cupola there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Was this photograph taken from the same side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from a different angle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: From a different angle, but from the same side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: No more questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi has also a question for you. JUDGE EL MAHDI: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] Could you please inform me on the basis of the photograph, that same photograph, yes, Exhibit P3753, and if I understood you correctly you said that this photograph, according to you, was taken from the part of the town that was under the control of the BH Army; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] During the period, that is, from September 1992 until August 1994, were you in a position to watch -- see the tower from that position? Let me explain myself. Were you in a position during that period of time to know what the damage was or the condition of the tower viewed from the side of the town that was controlled by the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was much closer to the church, some 30 to 50 metres away from where I was able to see it. But I wasn't able to see it from this position because it was held by the BH Army. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] You mean where the photo was taken, that was not under the control of the BH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The position from which the photograph was taken was under the control of the BH Army. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes. But to make it quite clear, you can't confirm that you were in a position to note the condition of the tower from the position held by the BH? I am trying to explain myself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am afraid I don't quite understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether one can hear the French channel. I think an error was made in the translation which is causing confusion. I don't know whether his Excellency is listening to the French channel. I don't know whether it was misinterpreted because I was listening to the other channel. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] I see. Thank you very much. What I am asking you, I am asking myself actually, I am wondering, how you can state what the exact condition of the tower was viewed from the area that was under the control of the other side, of the other party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should like to show you on the photograph where the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska was, where I was, when the tower of the church was devastated, and then probably things will become clearer. In front of the church and in front of this thicket there was a defence trench of the Army of Republika Srpska. It is about 30 to 50 metres from the church and one can see much better and clearer the damage done than from positions of the BH Army whose closest position was in this building and the side building attached. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] I see. So you were stationed close to the church; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have got one or more questions to you as well, Mr. DP9. You have answered questions in relation to the meeting that you had with the investigators of the Defence in the spring of this year. And you told us that you did not discuss with them matters such as confrontation lines at that very moment, but that they wanted to have your data and that they wanted to know whether you would be able to testify in The Hague. What did you discuss with them in respect of the content of your testimony, if you can answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they were interested in knowing in which part of the battlefield I was located in the period when combat operations were ongoing, and also whether I was willing to testify about that here in this court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you discussed with them where you were positioned during the armed conflict is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was globally speaking, whether I was on this side, on Grbavica but not actual positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say just the area where you were, where your unit was located during the armed conflict; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you go in any detail in other respects such as destruction of the church? Did you discuss that with them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. At the time I spent a short time with them. Believe me, I wouldn't even recognise them now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say "short time" can I think of 10 minutes, one hour, three hours? What should I understand by "a short time"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe some 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then you then only talked to in more detail when you arrived in The Hague; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had a more detailed discussion then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In between you had no other discussions with members of the Defence team, between this meeting of 20 minutes approximately and your arrival in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke to Madam Pilipovic in Kerac [phoen]. I was called up on the phone to check whether I had a passport, whether I would obtain a passport, and whether I could travel here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you then did not discuss the content of your testimony or did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't discuss the content of the testimony because I wasn't even sure that I would be coming. Everything was still uncertain at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell me, this first meeting of 20 minutes, did you take the initiative or were you approached by members of the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP9 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the Defence team came to see me because they had learned from some sources of their own and they wanted to ask me whether I would be willing to testify in The Hague Tribunal. I hadn't known them from before. And to tell you the truth, I was a bit surprised how they had come to see me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for your answers. Mr. DP9, this concludes your testimony in this court. We know it's a long way, and we know that you had to wait for a long time here. We would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague, because answers to questions of all parties and questions of the Bench are important for the determinations this Chamber will have to make. So I thank you again for coming to The Hague, for testifying, and I wish you a safe trip home again. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should also like to thank this Tribunal and all those present for the confidence shown in me and for the time they had spent and for the patience they had shown, and I hope I have been of a little assistance to this Tribunal which would give me a great deal of pleasure. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see you are on your feet, Mr. Ierace. What I would like to do first is deal with the documents with respect to DP9 and then I will give you an opportunity to deal with the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1769 under seal, pseudonym sheet; Exhibit D1770, map marked by witness; Exhibit D1771, map marked by witness; Exhibit P3753, black and white copies of five photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are there any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have an objection to make in principle but we believe that the justice has to follow its course. We believe that in spite of the fact that we were in some way obstructed in our proceedings, and we underscore this, and in the sense that many questions were asked by your Chamber about the position and the situation of the tower at the time of the events, we believe that we should not fight a lost battle but we believe that we were upset in the preparation of this, because it was the obligation, it was the obligation of the Prosecution to submit these documents. That was their duty of communication. Also the exculpatory evidence. Now, if the Prosecution wishes to withdraw this, that would be welcome. If not, we will -- we will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defect in procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please explain in perhaps 30 seconds again what exactly -- because I hear the Prosecution saying more or less that this is inculpatory evidence rather than exculpatory evidence. It is always nice that both parties see advantages in the material presented to the court. But what exactly makes this photographs of such a character -- that would make the -- that would put the Prosecution under the obligation to disclose them to you, since they had to consider them to be exculpatory.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. On several occasions we supported this position of the -- the support of the Prosecution thesis that this was just a sniper nest. This is what the Prosecution says, and I believe that was the case of the Prosecution. Now, if we had seen these photographs and if we had seen the practical impossibility during the time of the war for a man to hide himself behind the wall which didn't exist to use this position to shoot at anyone, then we would have asked these questions of the Prosecution witnesses bearing in mind that this point is something that could have been seen, that it would have been possible to see this sniper the moment that he climbed up there, he would have been seen. We were not able to ask these questions because these photographs were not shown to us. They were hidden from us. I have used up my 30 seconds. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understand what you mean. I think it would be wise to take a decision after the next break in respect of this objection. So, therefore the other exhibits are admitted into evidence, D1769 under seal, and that we still owe you a decision on 3753 and that's a Prosecution document. Then -- yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, as it happens, that was the topic that I wanted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I should have given you to opportunity to respond to the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's all right. Mr. President. Mr. President, I find it extraordinary for the Defence to suggest that these photographs should have been disclosed to them before they raised as an issue whether there was significant destruction to the bell tower. And in support of my position, I note that they maintain that the photographs are exculpatory. Mr. President, it wasn't until this morning that the Prosecution discovered that the crane which appears in the photograph was in fact there during the war. That was as a result of some enquiries made this morning, before court, just before court with some individuals in Sarajevo, namely, General Hadzic. So the position up until the last week was that there was no issue as to the condition of the tower, and then as a result of a letter sent to the Prosecution, we learn for the first time there is an issue, we go through our material, and we find that although we didn't have a photograph of the church during the conflict, the best we had was a photograph taken in August of 1996. And then this morning we discover in fact as it appears in this photograph in August of 1996, was the way it was during the war. There is nothing unreasonable about the position taken by the Prosecution in relation to these photographs in terms of disclosure. It simply reiterates the common sense behind the rules of the Tribunal that the Defence should make reasonable enquiries and make clear of what is an issue and what is not by compliance with Rule 90(H) during the Prosecution case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I granted you more time than I granted the Defence. But this will really be the last round. Let me just try to summarise. I do understand that the Prosecution says that this picture shows clearly that there was a position to fire from, let me use general terms, where the Defence says that this picture clearly shows that if you would be on that position, that you would be exposed to -- well, whatever kind of risks, and therefore, certainly would not be a position that you would fire from. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, no --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as we are concerned, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I don't know whether you meant to say it, Mr. President, but you sought to summarise the position of the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As far as inculpatory or exculpatory.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you look at the hole beneath the cupola, it appears to have even sides. Not the sort of hole one would expect from a tank shell. We don't accept that the tower was hit by a tank or that that hole was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am not saying, but let's just -- let's stay away from all the details of the damage done, but the relevant of the tower was such --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The relevance is whether this photograph appeared to a reasonable Prosecutor to depict shell damage. It does not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, what we are saying in relation to the production of the piece itself, of the exhibit itself, is that the Prosecution having possession of these documents and seeing them they could think that this was also the situation before, before the war. Before -- sorry, the Dayton Agreement. So what we are saying is that loyally, if the Prosecution had given this to us, then we would have been able to submit these documents to our witnesses during the preparation of the case. Looking at the facts, covering them immediately, and possibly examine, that is, cross-examine more profoundly the Prosecution witnesses in relation to the famous Dobrinja incidents. Now, the situation of the photographs is such that if this was how it was during the war, then they could have communicated them to us. If we had seen these photographs, the story would have been very different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, if I do rightly understand you, the position of the Defence is that if these documents, these photographs would have been known to the Defence, it might have given the Defence an opportunity to elicit exculpatory evidence from the potential witnesses. We will give you a decision after the break. The next witness to be called will be --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a witness without protective measures so we can give his name. This is Mr. Vukovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, could you please escort Mr. Vukovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gordan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, because I take it that you are Mr. Vukovic, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text of this declaration will be handed out to you now by the usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. Mr. Vukovic, you will first be examined by counsel for the Defence. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with your leave, I will begin the examination of this witness and then Madam Pilipovic will continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please approach the microphone so that we can hear you very well. Please. Thank you. Witness, could you please tell us what is your professional occupation?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I have a university degree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please be more precise.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I have a degree in political sciences in University of Sarajevo in 1984.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I have a request for Mr. Piletta-Zanin to move closer to the microphone as well, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps to put it on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I apologise. I was reading the questions on my computer. I will try. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your employment possibility at the end of your university studies?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't find a steady job. I was doing temporary jobs until about 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do then, please?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: In 1991, and there was a public announcement, for 1991, for admitting professional soldiers, contract soldiers, This was then several years before the war and I saw this as a possibility to find employment, to find a job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. From then, from when were you a professional soldier, from which moment?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I started to work from the 15th of January 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What was or what were at the time that you mentioned, what were the areas where you were quartered, where you were stationed?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I was at the Viktor Bubanj Barracks in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us in which part of the town, in which neighbourhood is Viktor Bubanj Barracks located?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: The Viktor Bubanj Barracks is located in the settlement of Svrakino Selo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us a little more about the location in terms of a municipality in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: This is the municipality, I think it is called Aneks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So we are absolutely certain about the location of this neighbourhood, this area was it near Novi Grad, Stari Grad, could you please just tell us little more about it, a little more details about it?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: This is municipality of Novi Grad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Witness, for how long did you stay in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I stayed there until the 2nd of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please repeat -- repeat the year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened on the 2nd of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Then from the superior command we received an order to go towards the main command which was located in Bistrik because it was surrounded by Muslim units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You say "we." When you say, "we," who do you mean exactly?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I mean the JNA, Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. At the time of these events, this Yugoslav People's Army, as you knew it in your department or in your company, what was its ethnic composition?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: It was multi-ethnic. It was a multi-ethnic unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please mention the ethnicities that you are aware of and whose members you saw in your unit?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can say that the commander of the unit, for instance, was a commander, his deputy a Muslim, his second deputy was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You indicated that this position was encircled by Muslim forces. Could you give us a little more details about this attack?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the main headquarters?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am referring to the second position that you indicated where you were meant to go to.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After the command, we had to retreat to Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the reason that you had to retreat?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: As the whole command had to withdraw, it was not able to do so because the column that was formed to move towards Lukavica was attacked by the Muslim army and we were captured there. We were imprisoned. And after two days of captivity, roughly, after an exchange that was arranged through UNPROFOR, we were transferred to Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you in any way whatsoever provoke that attack?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The forces that attacked you at the time, how were they organised as far as you were able to see, of course, that is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Prosecution objects again on the grounds of relevance given the pre-indictment period nature of this testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, I will respond gladly. The broad thesis of the Prosecution was that there was a plan prepared long ago that General Galic was the legitimate or illegitimate inheritor of that plan, and that he implemented. The submission, opposition of the defence is that not only there was no plan, but that what is more, the Muslim forces initiated plans against the Serbian forces. And I think this is quite in order. Perhaps we should have asked the witness to take off his headphones. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's not what you are asking the witness. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution's position is that whichever side initiated the armed conflict is of no relevance. The Prosecution has charged the accused with specific alleged unlawful acts in the conduct of the hostilities, not with who started or which parted started the hostilities. So for that reason, the Prosecution will renew its objection on the grounds of relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber deems that it is not without relevance. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, having listened to your explanation, I think the questions are related to, as you told us, plans and that would not, under all circumstances, require many details perhaps, but the objection is denied. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, these forces that were attacking your barracks or your military quarters, did they appear to you to be organised, well-structured? What can you tell us about them?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: In any event they were organised since they were able to attack a legal army, the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you speak of an attack did you suffer fire? Were you exposed to fire? Did you receive fire, incoming fire?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, fire was opened against us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this fire, for instance could you recognise it as coming from automatic weapons, weapons of war, in general terms?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: There was fire opened from automatic weapons and from Zoljas, hand-held rocket launchers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just checking, Mr. President, the translation. One of the translations I heard was a mortar. I heard a mortar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can we now focus on the question of uniforms. These persons who were attacking you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I think I give you some guidance how to deal with these issues. You are filling in what you heard on one of the translations. We still do not know, since it does not appear in the other translation. When you answered the question of the weapons used when fire was opened on you, what type of weapons did you mention?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mentioned automatic rifles and light hand-held rocket launchers that we call Zoljas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me come back to the question of uniforms. These forces that were attacking you, could they be recognised on the basis of the uniforms they wore or any kind of insignia or anything that they may have worn?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Most of the soldiers had camouflage uniforms with caps with ljiljans which was the insignia -- with lilies, which was the insignia of the Patriotic League which existed as a military formation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, under which conditions did you have to leave the barracks? When I say "conditions" I mean did you do it because you had to, did you have time to organise yourself or were you forced to leave?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: It was arranged with UNPROFOR that we should withdraw to Lukavica under their escort. In those days at the army command, the president at the time of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Alija Izetbegovic, arrived, and that should have been a guarantee for the safe withdrawal of the column from the barracks. Because it is well known that Muslims rarely respect agreements reached. And the president was supposed to have provided some sort of a guarantee that this would be observed, that the agreement would be observed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. During your urgent withdrawal, did you have time to empty the warehouses and to take with you the military materiel?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: No. We only took what we had at hand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what happened, if you know, with the military materiel that you were unable to take with you during the withdrawal?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: It fell into the hands of the Muslim units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I say "materiel" what exactly do you mean? Equipment? What exactly do you mean under that term?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Automatic rifles, pistols, hand-held launchers, Zoljas, and APCs that we had in our possession.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there also communication equipment?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there uniforms, too?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also protection material?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were some uniforms and also they took some uniforms off us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you talk about being captured, what was the treatment you were given?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Specifically in my case, I was treated with extreme brutality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us about that in this Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, again, this line of questions seems to the Prosecution to be irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Could we ask the witness -- may I ask you first, one thing: Do you understand any French or English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you to take your earphones off. Please, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. It is true, Mr. President, that the question of relevance of questions does not appear at first glance, but what is important is to know whether important violations of humanitarian law may have been committed in another place and whether this witness is aware of this. And this is a line of questioning which will lead us to reveal the brutality of treatment and the fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think no one stops you, unless you would like to -- yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The type of violations which were committed so that we might understand things properly, namely, Mr. President in relation to this essential question which is the alleged existence of a plan and the existence of a blind campaign of destruction, a random campaign of destruction that is alleged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, either immediately before the commencement of the Defence case or shortly after it commenced, the Prosecution filed a motion with respect to the Defence of tu quoque and/or reprisals. The Defence countered that that was not their intention, however, the first three or four lines of Mr. Piletta-Zanin's last response describes precisely the Defence of tu quoque, and I fail to see how, in the latter part of his answer, he made the link between the type of violations and the existence of a plan. That link is not clear in my mind and again it seems that notwithstanding the repeated denials of the Defence, that we are once again on the border of crossing into the -- what the Prosecution claims is a forbidden defence of tu quoque and/or reprisals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber does not understand the observations made by Mr. Piletta-Zanin as referring to tu quoque immediately. On the other hand, Mr. Piletta-Zanin you are asking about brutal treatment in an individual case outside the scope of the -- the time of the indictment period. The Chamber thinks that as such the relevance of that could be not very high. So if there is a link to the Defence you want to -- the line of the Defence, please come to your point then. Let's not stick into individual -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the question can be answered and then please come to come to your point or choose another line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite. Thank you very much. Mr. President I should like to underline the following: I never mentioned tu quoque, never. I never referred to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, the Chamber has not understood your observations as referring to tu quoque. So would the witness please put his headphones up again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, just in two or three words, could you tell us what was the treatment that you personally suffered on that occasion, and if you know, by your comrades.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I said that I personally was treated extremely brutally. Because when we were brought into the hall where we were held they brought with them a paper, an alleged statement that I was supposed to sign and which later on they would read on television or whenever they wanted to do with it. As I refused to sign it, then they took me to the basement of the building where they beat me virtually all night. And when I got there, I saw quite a number of other officers and soldiers that had been beaten and mistreated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My first question: What was the type of statement that they wanted you to sign? Could you tell us what it was about?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I am unable to say exactly because I refused to sign it. So they didn't let me read it even.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that statement was supposed to have been read or shown on a TV programme?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was probably meant to serve their propaganda that they used over the media throughout the war against us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I will move on to another subject. And that is, what view you had from certain windows of the barracks, what were you able to see from those windows from the barracks?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the Lukavica Barracks?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I am sorry. I am talking about the first barracks, the Bubanj Barracks.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: From the Viktor Bubanj Barracks, one could see Alipasino Polje and the Mojmilo hill above us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Before this period that we are referring to, that is immediately prior to the attack on the 2nd of May 1992, what were you able to notice on Mojmilo hill, please?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Towards the end of March and the beginning of April, we were able to see large groups of, males men, on Mojmilo hill engaging in some sort of works. Later on with binoculars, we were able to see them digging trenches. And talking to our superior officers, we learnt that they were digging trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be relatively precise regarding the dates? You said "end of March." Is that the date that you can confirm?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You indicated that these were groups of men. Do you know who they were? Were you able to identify who they were?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: As the distance was large, it was not possible to identify them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And those groups were they groups that one could recognise as belonging to a particular structure?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: With the help of binoculars, one could notice on some of the soldiers insignia, the insignia of the Patriotic League, so they were obviously Muslim formations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you simply describe the insignia for us very briefly?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: When I say "insignia of the Patriotic League" it is the present day marks or badges used by Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is, the badge with the lilies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Let us now move on to Lukavica. Could you tell us from the time when you were evacuated to Lukavica, what rank did you have and what position did you hold?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: In Lukavica I was an ordinary soldier, and as I had been hurt, injured, I was relieved of certain activities. So I mainly worked in logistics and I did guard duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you spoke of logistics, can you be more precise?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Actually I was in charge of the equipment in the possession of our company or rather our battalion in Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what your military unit was that you belonged to at that moment?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: It was the Military Police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So you're testifying that you engaged in activities of the police, that you served in the police?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you engage in police investigations, for the army of course?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: With respect to the soldiers, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, your group or team of policemen, did you have to intervene sometimes if a soldier committed acts which were not in conformity with the rules or military ethics?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: There were such cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when such cases occurred were you in a position to have sanctions declared and possibly actually implemented?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you have occasion to visit locations close to the front or on the front during the period when you were at Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us until when you stayed at Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I stayed in Lukavica until the 17th of October, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Throughout that period of your stay there, were you able, now with greater precision please, visit locations of fire, firing positions? I am talking about heavy weapons.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the line of questions that we are going to put now will refer to heavy weapons. Maybe it is the time for the break. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say heavy weapons take more time than light weapons. Yes. We will adjourn until ten minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber owes the party still a decision on the P Exhibit, the photographs on the church. It will be given at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you,

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just to use the opportunity of the break, we wanted to show a tape now, and the number that was given was 34812. The Prosecution had received this tape as well as the translation of the transcript, and we would ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We wanted the technical booth to start with the very first segment and then the very last. So if we can start with the very first excerpt and then if we can fast forward to the very last segment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution objects to the showing of the videotape on two grounds. First --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we deal with it in the presence of the witness or should we ask him to take his earphones off?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I just perhaps give you in the briefest possible terms the grounds, then we can determine if that might be necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If you can do it in such a way then -- one moment please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution objects on the grounds of relevance, and if the Trial Chamber were to have the benefit of the transcript, the Prosecution asserts that it would become quite apparent that the tape is, in our submission, irrelevant, and also we would object on the grounds that no foundation has been laid with the current witness for the showing of the videotape and in the absence of such a proper foundation, the Prosecution suggests that the tape should not be shown. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I ask you to take your headphones off. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you perhaps first answer the last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Gladly. As far as the second reason is concerned, that is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... to respond to the last issue, and the last issue that there was no relation with this witness. So that is -- so that's not about relevance, that is -- we don't have to read the transcript, but what is the relation? What do you show the tape to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but that is exactly what I was going to say, Mr. President, just to respond to the very last question. If we view this tape, we will know why. We will see the barracks in question, that is the Viktor Bubanj Barracks at the time when it was attacked, and we will also see, which is very important, this witness because I cannot point to him because that will give him ideas. I don't want to give his name. But we will see him among the prisoners. And that is important that in relation to his credibility that he is telling us things that are real. These are things that happened. But not only this. What is important to see is the situation, the state of these people and not for any kind of tu quoque defence but this tape which is a historical tape, doesn't give us an image of an aggressor's army but the reality is, these are soldiers, conscripts that were ambushed exiting the barracks. And that is extremely important in terms of strategic questions. Because if the plan was made then, then we would have expected armed combatants, armed to the teeth, and I believe that justice should be able to view it properly. That's as far as the second point is concerned. And I am going to stop here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time does the tape take?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It very brief. We are just talking about a few minutes, Mr. President. And only a few seconds for some other excerpts, so it is not a very long video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We did allow questions to the witness in respect of the attack before. It would be inconsistent not to allow then further clarification of this. We allow that as you heard, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, in respect of what was the plan and that much details perhaps would not be necessary under all circumstances. If it is just a couple of minutes. But one of the things -- I do understand that it is not tu quoque. It is not as I understand part of a Defence of self-defence; is that correct? Is my understanding correct? So it's just a demonstration as you tell us to give an impression of the state in which soldiers at that time found themselves in order to demonstrate that this is not a situation where a plan was waged or that -- I do understand you well. Yes. Okay. Then the technical booth asks you not to say that you want to see the first and the last sequence, but how many sequences are there between the first and the last?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I propose that we proceed in the following manner: We have the distribution but I don't know whether it corresponds to the excerpts. Can we start with the tape and then if I say stop, we can fast forward to the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The better way of doing this is to prepare it with the technicians before. We will see how much time it takes and we will then see. So let's start with the tape and you give clear instructions, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, to the booth. Please do it in English. That might be easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. If we at the beginning of the tape, could we please start the tape with a normal speed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: "At the 2nd Army District Command damages caused by yesterday's attack that lasted until afternoon and evening are more than visible. Here, shoot this horror... Lead the reporters on. Please film all this. Colonel, what happened here? Here have a look at it all."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I would like the tape to continue, please. Could we please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: "The following private soldiers have been identified. Slobodan Jelic, Predrag Cerovic, Srecko Jovanovic, Miodrag Dzurovic, Zdravko Tomovic. Several other soldiers have not been identified. Lethal wounds were inflicted by the shrapnel from an exploded mine, bullets fired by hand firearms fired at close range. Colonel Dr. Budimir Radulovic has been killed with a shot fired at the back of his head, while he was seated in the back of an ambulance bearing clear Red Cross markings. Colonel Miro Sokic has been killed by a bullet fired to his head from a distance not greater than 50 centimetres. Colonel Gradimir Petrovic was killed with a shot to his back. Colonel Enes Tasso and about a dozen soldiers have been heavily wounded. "About 120 JNA soldiers have been taken prisoner. Several JNA officers have taken part in the assassination and taking prisoner of the JNA soldiers, namely Captain Refik Cesko and Lieutenant-Colonel Esad Tokic and that deserted the 2nd Army District Command together with Colonel Vehbija Karic."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That will be all. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we just saw a clip, a video clip. Can you confirm these facts as they were shown on video?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. More precisely, these persons that we see seated, did you know them? Is this a location where you were?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: This is the location where I was, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you among these people, among these men?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We were told of a number of officers who were killed. Could you please tell us how these people were killed -- how these men were killed, if you know?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Some were killed when the convoy was attacked, when it left the army district command, when the shooting started. Some of them were in the lorry, some of them were in the cars and then they were shot at and they were killed and some were even in ambulance vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that they were shot while they were inside ambulances?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I would like to come back to the line of questioning earlier about heavy weapons. Were you able to visit some sites, battery sites of mortars, grenade launchers; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Some of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, in a general way did it happen that the soldiers would get drunk, that they would get intoxicated, drink more than normal?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: There were such cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, if this took considerable proportions in terms of duty what was the response of your police force, of your police service?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: If they were too aggressive, then we had a detention place they would be taken, and they would stay there for a night until they calmed down. And if they weren't too aggressive, they would be taken to the barracks to sober up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If a soldier came to his post that drunk, that is incapable of doing anything whatsoever that would be reasonable and that you knew of that, what would have been or what would be the response of your service? What measure, if any, would you have taken?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Our measure was to take him off the post, of the position, because if he was in that state he would not be able to carry out his duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that what the instruction said from your military hierarchy?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: That was the instructions that we received from the superior command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. With respect to these instructions in the army, were there instructions with respect to the problems of civilians, the shooting, the firing, and the civilians?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what were these instructions, what kind of instructions were they?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: We received instructions from the immediate superiors, that is, from our company commander, from the battalion commander, and the instructions they received from the Corps Commander, and this was a written order that they received which was not to fire at civilians and civilian facilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the frequency that these orders, if ever, were repeated?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: These -- they were repeated most often at unit meetings, which means once a week. Because there would be many new soldiers coming, so there was a need to repeat this order, to bear it in mind all the time, since if something unexpected happened so that the other side, the opposing side, wouldn't make use of it from media point of view.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You are speaking about new soldiers. Did any orders come about the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Inversely, Witness, if the soldiers didn't respect these orders, if, I am saying "if," would you have been able to find that out, to know this?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: If the orders were not respected, then we did [Realtime transcript read in error "didn't"] know about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Did it occur, and I am speaking in general, I am not talking about the problem of shooting, but did it ever happen in general that soldiers would not carry out certain orders or they would carry them out badly, deliberately, would you then be able to intervene?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: When we are talking about my unit, there were no such --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just ask for a clarification. The question was put to you that if -- no -- yes. If the soldiers would not respect these orders, orders about not aiming at civilians, and it was repeated, "if," would you have been able to find that out, to know this? What was your answer to that question? I am just asking you to repeat your question [sic] because there might be a translation problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we found out about such a thing, then we would undertake certain measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you find out? The question was -- your answer started with: "If the orders were not respected," and then did you say you would find out or that you would not find out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would find out for some.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I was listening to the French channel and that is what I understood the answer to be, where in the English translation, I find the opposite. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed. Indeed. Thank you for this correction. I was hearing the Serbian and the French and I didn't notice the transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I am asking the question in relation to other units, Witness. Did you hear that colleagues who had the same duties as you did, that these were Military Policemen, that they could have been taking sanctions with respect to other units, intervening with respect to other units?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I now would like to come back to the instructions that were given with respect to opening of fire. If you know that instructions were given to open fire as a rule, only as returning fire, as a response?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: That was a strict order just to open fire in response to fire being opened against us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke about -- I am sorry. You spoke about the logistics earlier, Witness. Would this also include ammunition?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, in relation to the control of the ammunition, what could you tell the Chamber particularly with respect to the opening of fire, and I am talking about small arms fire and later we can talk about heavy weapons.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of the control ammunition, that is the quantities that could be used, quantities of ammunition that could be use would respect to small arms, were there any instructions that were given to you by the command in terms of logistics, in terms of economising on the ammunition, and so on?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were certain instructions given specifically from the superiors. We were told what the quantity of ammunition is to be issued to certain units. I would receive this order and I would carry it out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Was this the same situation, and I am talking about economising on the ammunition, when we are talking about heavy weapons, artillery in particular, if you know?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you think so?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't have -- I mean, we didn't have too much ammunition so the order was given to strictly respect it, every bullet, every grenade had to be justified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Since we are talking about weapons and ammunition -- no, I withdraw that. Let us leave the area of ammunition. And I would like, Witness, if you can tell us, if in the area that you knew, destructions occurred? And when I talk about destructions, I mean buildings, all different buildings, civilian, military and so on.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What scope was the destruction, please?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: The destruction was large, large-scale. As far as we could see, there was a great deal of damage more to civilian facilities as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How can you explain the fact that important damage was done to civilian facilities?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps the witness could be asked to clarify. It is a bit unclear from the record exactly which area the witness is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. It is not clear on whether we are talking about damages on one or the other side of the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am talking of the zone that the witness was familiar with as a soldier. So I am talking about from May 1992 to October 1993, the area that he was in as a soldier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's different. If you just have asked it to the witness because you very often ask witnesses about damage on the other side of the confrontation line rather than their own side. So, instead of justifying yourself, you perhaps ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I am starting with this side and then I will go on to the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on your side what was the damage inflicted? Was that your answer? Were you referring to your side of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my second question is the following: How can you explain these large-scale damages to civilian property?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: In this part of the town where the barracks was is the part of Dobrinja under the control of our forces. And the Muslims attempted several attacks across the confrontation line, and they often opened fire from infantry weapons as well as from artillery weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which were the artillery weapons used?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Most frequently they used anti-aircraft machine-guns, and I think there were also tanks and mortars used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you mentioned mortars, what calibre did the BH Army have in their possession?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I am unable to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the number of tanks that the BH forces had in their possession, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I would not be able to give you a precise answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know from where fire was opened on Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: They opened fire from Mojmilo hill and Dobrinja, the part of Dobrinja under their control and from a barracks, Jusuf Dzonlic, Barracks Jusuf Dzonlic on Alipasino Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they open fire on several occasions?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Throughout the period when you were at Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, we will continue with this line of questioning. Regarding the damage itself, and I am referring in general terms to Sarajevo, could you tell us where the greatest damage was, in general terms?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection. No foundation has been laid for this type of question, Mr. President. He is talking in terms of the entire city of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, a person who lived for a certain number of years in Sarajevo and who had the position of a police officer, has information as a professional, as a man, as a soldier, and this information is invaluable. I don't think it is necessary to have all these elements to be able to answer a question of principle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether this is a question of principle where the greatest damage was in general terms. It seems to me rather a question of facts. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, when asking the witness, could you ask him about the source of his knowledge and perhaps also in view of time, because I did hear that he was evacuated at a certain moment. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone. Microphone. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to the question that we would like to put to you, and that is: Where, mainly, was the greatest amount of destruction in Sarajevo, if you know that? How do you know that? What are your sources, that would be my first question.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Large-scale damage was inflicted on the part of Dobrinja under our control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am interrupting you. Before answering, how did you come to know what you are now perhaps going to tell us? Where is the -- what is the origin of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I was on the spot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But as for other parts of Sarajevo, did you know about them?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: As regards other parts of Sarajevo, I knew it on the basis of information we received from other persons, from our superiors and from other soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may continue, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, but this is -- this would, unless there are reasons for you to say otherwise, hearsay as such is not inadmissible. But of course the source of the hearsay, if there would be better evidence to assess the reliability of this information other sources would have to be preferred, as you will understand. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please answer the question regarding the zone you are familiar with, that is Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Regarding Dobrinja, the part of Dobrinja that was under Serbian control, we went there a couple of times to Dobrinja. We had some interventions to do there, and we could see destruction done to civilian facilities and the church that was located there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And this destruction, was it mostly close to the lines; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat his answer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We didn't hear the answer to the question by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry. I am going to ask him to repeat his answer. But I think I heard him say yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if we ask a witness to repeat a certain answer because the translation has not been complete, I guided you several times that it is not up to you to tell us already what you heard the answer was. Would you please refrain from that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us the sources of your information. What happened, Witness, with the people who fled from the parts of Sarajevo that were under BH control?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: There was a lot of fleeing and they would come to the command for an information interview.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you are talking about "information interviews" was this intelligence work; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that basis, were you also able to obtain strategic and intelligence information?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes one could collect quite a lot of information in this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this kind of information could it refer to certain facilities in the town of Sarajevo under BH control?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can understand that you have concern about confidentiality, but without violating your duty, are you talking about military targets?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Were there many such people who were bringing information with them?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Dragonov; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I should now like to ask you a certain number of questions concerning the situation of civilian areas that were not under BH control. In those areas, were there any systems of protection for civilians, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was a system of protection. Specifically, in front of the barracks, there was a protection against infantry weapons. So the protective devices had to be put up so they wouldn't be hit by the opposing force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Describe that protection. What did it consist of?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: At first there were sandbags and later on when fire was stronger, there were pipes that were laid along the road to protect both vehicles and civilians from enemy fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you talk about enemy fire, what can you tell us about the frequency of combat in the zone you were familiar with? Were they frequent conflicts? What type of weapons were used?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: The fighting was frequent. Infantry weapons were used most, coupled with anti-aircraft guns and heavy machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke of protection in the area of Lukavica. Do you know whether there was such protection in other areas?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: In the zones I went to, there was protection, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What zones are you referring to and what type of protection, please?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I am talking about Grbavica, Vraca and a part of Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And what type of protection?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: There was protection consisting of sandbags, old vehicles, something that would provide protection to civilians against enemy fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the question may be obvious for you, but not for me. From which did the civilians in this part of the town that you are referring to want to protect themselves?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: They sought to protect themselves from enemy fire, from infantry weapons and...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you talk about enemy fire, are you referring only to infantry weapons, but also to some other weapons, as your answer wasn't quite finished?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us which weapons?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: We knew that the enemy side had heavy weapons, and we had to take steps to protect ourselves of that type of projectiles coming from heavy weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And were such -- was such fire from heavy weapons frequent?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Quite frequent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In each of the zones that you mentioned, are you referring to all the zones that you have listed?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you personally know any civilians who suffered as a result of this fire coming either from infantry or artillery weapons?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I did see quite a lot of people who were wounded with fire from infantry and artillery weapons but I couldn't remember their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "several" according to an estimate of the number of civilians wounded, would you say that they were many or that they were an exception, if you could tell us?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: There were many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, let us now pass on to another point and that is some geographical issues. What could you tell us regarding the features, the elevated features, the following ones: Zuc, Mojmilo, Hum, Kobilja Glava, and the wood, and Zuc, Mojmilo and Hum. Let me repeat myself.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: These are elevations used by the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sedam Suma, the Seven Woods area, do you know who was in that zone?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't give you an answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As regards the other two that I mentioned, the small and the high?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colina Kapa?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that either. No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will move on, Witness. And I would like to ask you something about relationships with UNPROFOR. As a police officer, Military Police officer were you informed of problems that arose in connection with the transport conducted by UN forces and which may have contained some smuggled goods, military goods intended for one or other side?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I personally was not informed about that. Or could you be more precise, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will be glad to. My question was badly worded and I apologise for this. Does the name "Oxygen" does it ring a well? A code name "Oxygen"?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that there was arms trafficking organised, and if yes, what can you tell us about it or the smuggling of weapons?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: I heard stories about that, but I couldn't give you a specific answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the basis of the information that you were able to collect from these examinations, did you know whether the BH forces had mobile mortars? They are mortars mounted on small lorries that could be easily moved around depending on needs or the will of the persons using them.

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to confront the stories that you heard from these different people to corroborate the truth of what you heard?

utterances.speaker: GORDAN VUKOVIC
utterances.text: We had several reports which we compared amongst themselves later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. What could you tell us, Witness, about the enclave of certain areas that remained under the control of the Serb authorities in Sarajevo? I am referring, for instance, to Grbavica and some other such enclave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It is not clear, Mr. President, what that question is going to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would be glad to. Witness will you please remove your headphones. Mr. President, one of the submissions of the Prosecution is to assert that Sarajevo was a town under siege, and that it was arbitrarily attacked by Serb forces from the heights. What we wish to prove is the thesis of partition and saying that on the Serb side there were pockets from which the people could no longer leave. And I think that this is an important element.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think -- it is not relevance that Mr. Mundis is complaining about, objecting against, but that the question was not clear, that you could not know what answer to what question an answer would be given to. Your question was, you asked first about mortars mounted on small lorries, whether he had any knowledge about that. The answer was "yes." Then your next question was: "Were you able to confront the stories that you heard from these different people to corroborate the truth of what you heard?" So I take it that is still about mobile mortars. Then the next question was: "What could you tell us, Witness, about the enclave of certain areas that remained under the control of the Serb authorities of Sarajevo? I am referring to Grbavica and some other such enclave." It is not clear to Mr. Mundis, and I share his view, what you are actually asking the witness. So could you please clarify what specifically you want to know from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, what I don't understand is why you referred to my two previous questions that have nothing to do with this. It is a completely different line of questioning. I have ended with the mortars. What I wanted to know is what the witness knows --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What the witness knows about what?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am going to tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you ask it in such a way that Mr. Mundis understand it, that I understand it, then there would be a fair chance that the witness would understand it as well. We will have to adjourn anyhow. So you have a lot of hours' time unless you would like to put the question to the witness now, you can do it. But otherwise in reformulating your question, you have a couple of hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was just informed that not as it is usual, this courtroom will be used again at a quarter past 2.00, but already at 2.00. So I must -- although I gave you an opportunity to reformulate your question, I'd invite you to do that tomorrow. If you want to tender the videotape would you please give it a number so that we can decide on it tomorrow. Since this courtroom will be used at 2.00, we will adjourn until tomorrow morning at 9.00 and then we will continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
